english: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be the roots of the equation $x^{3}-3x^{2}+1=0$. Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be the points whose position vectors with respect to the origin $O$ are $\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+\alpha^{3}\hat{k}$, $\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+\beta^{3}\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i}+\gamma\hat{j}+\gamma^{3}\hat{k}$, respectively. Then the volume of the tetrahedron $OABC$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ समीकरण $x^{3}-3x^{2}+1=0$ के मूल हैं। माना कि $A$, $B$, $C$ वे बिन्दु हैं जिनके मूलबिन्दु $O$ के सापेक्ष स्थिति सदिश क्रमशः $\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+\alpha^{3}\hat{k}$, $\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+\beta^{3}\hat{k}$ तथा $\hat{i}+\gamma\hat{j}+\gamma^{3}\hat{k}$ हैं। तब चतुष्फलक $OABC$ का आयतन ______ है।
solution_full: For a tetrahedron with one vertex at the origin, volume $=\dfrac{1}{6}\left|\left[\overrightarrow{OA}\ \overrightarrow{OB}\ \overrightarrow{OC}\right]\right|$, and the scalar triple product is the determinant of the components:
Subtracting the first row from the second and third rows: $R_2-R_1$ gives $(0,\ \beta-\alpha,\ \beta^3-\alpha^3)$ and $R_3-R_1$ gives $(0,\ \gamma-\alpha,\ \gamma^3-\alpha^3)$.

Taking the factors $(\beta-\alpha)$ and $(\gamma-\alpha)$ out of these rows: $\Delta=(\beta-\alpha)(\gamma-\alpha)\begin{vmatrix}1&\beta^2+\alpha\beta+\alpha^2\\1&\gamma^2+\alpha\gamma+\alpha^2\end{vmatrix}$.

For the product of differences write $f(x)=x^3-3x^2+1=(x-\alpha)(x-\beta)(x-\gamma)$. Differentiating the product and putting $x=\alpha$ gives $f'(\alpha)=(\alpha-\beta)(\alpha-\gamma)$; similarly $f'(\beta)=(\beta-\alpha)(\beta-\gamma)$ and $f'(\gamma)=(\gamma-\alpha)(\gamma-\beta)$.

Now $f'(x)=3x^2-6x=3x(x-2)$, so $f'(\alpha)f'(\beta)f'(\gamma)=27\,\alpha\beta\gamma\,(\alpha-2)(\beta-2)(\gamma-2)$. Here $\alpha\beta\gamma=-1$ and $(\alpha-2)(\beta-2)(\gamma-2)=-f(2)=-(8-12+1)=3$, so the product is $-81$.
Hence $\left[(\alpha-\beta)(\beta-\gamma)(\gamma-\alpha)\right]^2=81$ and $|(\alpha-\beta)(\beta-\gamma)(\gamma-\alpha)|=9$ (the roots are real and distinct).
originality_note: New: the vertices are points (1, t, t^3) at the three roots of a cubic, so the volume is a generalized Vandermonde determinant (a-b)(b-c)(c-a)(a+b+c) whose size is fixed by the discriminant and the sum of roots (way 5). Closest known: volume of a tetrahedron from given position vectors; the textbook factorisation of the (1, a, a^3) determinant. Different because: the roots are never found; the volume comes from symmetric functions through the discriminant.

concept_use.Application of Scalar triple product: Volume of tetrahedron OABC = (1/6)|[OA OB OC]|, written as the 3x3 determinant of components.
concept_use.Application of properties of determinant: Row operations and factor theorem reduce the determinant to (beta-alpha)(gamma-alpha)(gamma-beta)(alpha+beta+gamma).

The cubic has three distinct real roots (discriminant 81), so A, B, C exist and the volume does not depend on the order of the roots. Changed: No change.
key_step: Factorising the (1, t, t^3) determinant as product of differences times the sum, then the product of differences from f'(alpha)f'(beta)f'(gamma) with f' = 3x(x-2).
justification: Two linked ideas: determinant factorisation by properties and the discriminant via symmetric functions, with no roots available; numerical format, no options. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q12 (L4) in using triple-product algebra, but each step here is standard coaching material, so L3 as 2021-P1-Q19 (L3).
